nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a list of distinct positive natural numbers, $t$ a positive natural number, and $r$ the value returned by the exact subset sum algorithm on $x$ with target $t$. Then $r$ is the sum of some sublist of $x$ (a subsequence, not necessarily contiguous), $r \le t$, and every sublist of $x$ whose sum is at most $t$ has sum at most $r$.
nodes.title: Optimality of exact subset sum for distinct positive inputs

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a list of natural numbers, $t$ a natural number, and $r$ the value returned by the exact subset sum algorithm on $x$ with target $t$. Then $r$ is the sum of some sublist of $x$ (a subsequence, not necessarily contiguous), $r \le t$, and every sublist of $x$ whose sum is at most $t$ has sum at most $r$.
nodes.title: Optimality of exact subset sum

nodes.summary: For every list $x$ of natural numbers and every natural number $t$, the value returned by the exact subset sum algorithm on $x$ with target $t$ equals $\max(\cdots\max(\max(0, s_1), s_2)\cdots, s_k)$, where $s_1, \dots, s_k$ is the final list of sums computed by the exact subset sum traversal on $x$ with target $t$.
nodes.title: Exact subset sum returns the maximum of the computed sums

nodes.summary: For every list $x$ of natural numbers, of length $n$, and every natural number $t$, the final list of sums computed by the exact subset sum traversal on $x$ with target $t$ has length at most $2^n$.
nodes.title: The number of computed sums is at most two to the power of the input length

nodes.summary: For every list $x$ of natural numbers with sum $S$ and every natural number $t$, the final list of sums computed by the exact subset sum traversal on $x$ with target $t$ has length at most $S + 1$.
nodes.title: The number of computed sums is at most the input total plus one

nodes.summary: For every list $x$ of natural numbers and every natural number $t$, the final list of sums computed by the exact subset sum traversal on $x$ with target $t$ has length at most $t + 1$.
nodes.title: The number of computed sums is at most the target plus one

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a list of natural numbers, $t$ a natural number, and $L$ the final list of sums computed by the exact subset sum traversal on $x$ with target $t$. A natural number $z$ belongs to $L$ if and only if $z \le t$ and $z$ is the sum of some sublist of $x$ (a subsequence, not necessarily contiguous).
nodes.title: Characterization of the exact subset sum list

nodes.summary: Let $i \le n$ be natural numbers. On the list $1, 2, 4, \dots, 2^{i-1}$ (the first $i$ entries of $1, 2, \dots, 2^{n-1}$) with target $2^n - 1$, the final list of sums computed by the exact subset sum traversal is exactly $0, 1, 2, \dots, 2^i - 1$ in increasing order.
nodes.title: Prefixes of the powers of two attain every sum

nodes.summary: For every list $x$ of natural numbers and every natural number $t$, the final list of sums computed by the exact subset sum traversal on $x$ with target $t$ is strictly increasing; in particular it has no repeated entries.
nodes.title: The exact subset sum list is strictly increasing

nodes.summary: For every list $x$ of natural numbers and every natural number $t$, the final list of sums computed by the exact subset sum traversal on $x$ with target $t$ contains $0$.
nodes.title: Zero is always a computed sum

nodes.summary: Given a list $x = (x_1, \dots, x_n)$ of natural numbers and a target $t \in \mathbb{N}$, this timed procedure starts from the list $L_0 = (0)$ and, for $i = 1, \dots, n$ in order, forms $L_i$ from $L_{i-1}$ in four steps: add $x_i$ to every entry of $L_{i-1}$; merge $L_{i-1}$ with this shifted list (the standard merge of two lists, comparing entries with $\le$); delete adjacent repeated values; and keep only the…
nodes.title: Attainable sums in exact subset sum

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the exact subset-sum procedure on the list $(2^0, 2^1, \dots, 2^{n-1})$ (empty when $n = 0$) with target $2^n - 1$ makes at least $2^n - 1$ counted events.
nodes.title: Exponential lower bound for exact subset sum on powers of two

nodes.summary: For every list $x$ of $n$ natural numbers and every target $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the exact subset-sum procedure on $x$ and $t$ makes at most $1 + n + 7(2^n - 1) + 2^n$ counted events.
nodes.title: Exponential upper bound for exact subset sum

nodes.summary: For every list $x$ of $n$ natural numbers with sum $s$ and every target $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the exact subset-sum procedure on $x$ and $t$ makes at most $1 + n + (7n + 1)\min(t + 1, s + 1)$ counted events.
nodes.title: Pseudo-polynomial bound for exact subset sum

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a list of $n$ natural numbers and let $t, d \in \mathbb{N}$ with $t \le n^d$. Then the exact subset-sum procedure on $x$ and $t$ makes at most $1 + n + (7n + 1)(n^d + 1)$ counted events.
nodes.title: Polynomial event bound for exact subset sum with a polynomially bounded target

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a list of $n$ natural numbers and let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ be such that every entry of $x$ is at most $n^d$. Then for every target $t \in \mathbb{N}$ the exact subset-sum procedure on $x$ and $t$ makes at most $1 + n + (7n + 1)(n \cdot n^d + 1)$ counted events.
nodes.title: Polynomial event bound for exact subset sum with polynomially bounded inputs

nodes.summary: Let $x = (x_1, \dots, x_n)$ be a list of natural numbers and $t \in \mathbb{N}$ a target. For $0 \le i \le n$ let $L_i$ be the list of attainable sums of the prefix $(x_1, \dots, x_i)$ with target $t$. For $i < n$ let $M_i$ be the merge of $L_i$ with the list obtained by adding $x_{i+1}$ to every entry of $L_i$, let $c_i$ be the number of comparisons this merge makes, and let $D_i$ be $M_i$ with adjacent repeated…
nodes.title: Event count of exact subset sum

nodes.summary: Given a list $x$ of natural numbers and a target $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the procedure first computes the list $L = (\ell_1, \dots, \ell_m)$ of attainable sums of $x$ with target $t$, then scans it from left to right, keeping a running maximum that starts at $0$, and returns $\max(0, \ell_1, \dots, \ell_m)$. Its counted events are those of computing $L$ plus one per entry of $L$.
nodes.title: Exact subset sum procedure

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
